newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army deserters return under amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army deserters return under amnesty.

text.p: Almost 20,000 deserters from Sri Lanka's depleted army have returned under a six-month amnesty which expired on Saturday, a military spokesman said on Monday.
"We had a very good response to our amnesty, especially in the last few days," Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters. "We expect more to trickle in from remote areas."
Forcing deserters to return to barracks is part of the military's plan to beef up the forces, who have been fighting the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam for 13 years.
The army has an approved strength of 100,000 but many battalions are under strength because of battle casualties, desertions and retirements.

More than 4,000 deserters reported to army camps, police stations and government officials in charge of village administration on the last day of the amnesty which has been extended several times since June, Jayatunga said.
The army and police also arrested more than 1,800 deserters, he said.

The military has said it will crack down on deserters who failed to respond, but has so far not indicated what punishment awaits them. The government has also warned firms against employing deserters.
The army was forced to extend the amnesty several times to get back deserters because of poor responses to its recriuitment drives, officials said.
The government has said it is considering introducing conscription to get the required numbers for the army if the amnesties and recruitment drives fail.
Many soldiers go absent without leave after being deployed for months without a break in the war zone or because of poor pay.

According to defence ministry figures, about 15,000 soldiers have deserted during the past five years when fighting escalated with the rebels, who are seeking an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
